BEST_BASELINE.note: shipped defaults: MiniLM encoder, pool 48, mdeberta reader fp32

BEST_EXPERIMENT.status: VALIDATED BUT NOT ADOPTED - blocked on a scope decision, see blocked_on
BEST_EXPERIMENT.note: multilingual-e5-small with query:/passage: prefixes, EMBEDDING_MAX_TOKENS=512, RAG_CANDIDATE_POOL_SIZE=256, HNSW_EF_SEARCH=400
blocked_on: infra/live/{develop,prod}/main.tf must name the same model the Dockerfile bakes (pinned by tests/unit/test_embedding_config_matches_image.py). infra/ is outside the agreed scope boundary.
Adopting it DELETES and re-embeds every stored chunk: same 384 width, different vector space. That is a production data operation, not a config flip.

rejected_this_iteration.pool_256_alone: Measured under the shipped MiniLM encoder: MLQA-en R@10 80.5 -> 82.5, MLQA-vi 56.5 -> 56.0, ViQuAD 68.8 -> 70.2, for ~+400ms retrieval p50. Vietnamese got worse. The pool gain only materialises with a retrieval-trained encoder, so it was reverted rather than shipped on English-only evidence.
rejected_this_iteration.removing_vector_distance_threshold: Byte-identical results under e5 (the cutoff is inert: all 48 candidates already pass). Destructive under MiniLM (0/60 gold chunks passed), but that is fixed by the encoder, not by the threshold. No change made.
rejected_this_iteration.fusion_weights_iter4: Down-weighting the no-IDF sparse leg to dense/sparse 1.0/0.25 gave BYTE-IDENTICAL retrieval metrics to the 1.0/1.0 control on both Vietnamese splits (120 q each): MLQA-vi R@10 58.33 both, ViQuAD-vi R@10 72.73 both. Root cause in code: SearchService re-scores fused candidates with the lexical reranker and sorts by that (search_service.py:199), discarding the RRF order, so fusion weights are inert until the reranker is replaced. RAG_FUSION_*_WEIGHT kept as inert 1.0/1.0 knobs; nothing shipped.
rejected_this_iteration.cross_encoder_reranker_iter5: bge-reranker-v2-m3 (Apache-2.0, multilingual, CPU ONNX) built as src/lib/reranker/ behind RERANKER_BACKEND (default lexical). It fixes ranking quality (an inspected MLQA-vi query moved gold rank 6->1; answer_in_context 70->75 at n=20) but end-to-end MLQA-vi F1 was IDENTICAL to lexical (35.30 == 35.30, gate off), because the reader's gold-context ceiling (61.4) is binding, not retrieval ranking. Costs 6x retrieval latency (8.5s vs 1.4s/q, fp32 568M on CPU). Kept as opt-in off-by-default capability, not adopted. Two score-scale calibration bugs found and fixed en route (RAG_MIN_RELEVANCE_SCORE and RAG_MIN_CONTEXT_SCORE both assumed the lexical 0..1 range).
rejected_this_iteration.xlmr_large_viquad_reader_iter6: NamSyntax/xlmr-large-viquad (Apache-2.0, XLM-R-Large fine-tuned on ViQuAD 2.0) exported to ONNX and tested. Gold-context ceiling: +2.8 F1 on CLEAN MLQA-vi, +14.6 on in-domain ViQuAD-vi, but -16.5 on MLQA-en (VI specialist, wrecks English). END-TO-END on clean MLQA-vi: WORSE than mDeBERTa (F1 35.30 -> 30.23, EM 25 -> 5), gate-off only 32.05 so not a calibration artifact -- xlmr's ViQuAD span conventions misalign with MLQA boundaries (EM collapse). REJECTED: research promised F1 ~88, clean end-to-end test overturned it. Third reader rejected after int8 and XLM-R-base.

target.binding_constraint: reader quality on Vietnamese. Gold-context ceiling measured at 61.4 F1 (MLQA-vi) and 56.3 (ViQuAD-vi) - both below 90 before retrieval is even considered. Published extractive SOTA is 75.2 (MLQA-vi) and 77.24 (UIT-ViQuAD 2.0).
